reports.text: Outside study ordered by neurology, copy to PCP. Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without contrast. Generalized parenchymal volume loss with disproportionate atrophy of both hippocampi. Scattered small foci of white matter T2 hyperintensity typical for age. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No mass, hemorrhage or extra-axial collection. Ventricles proportionate to sulci. Major flow voids preserved.
reports.conclusion: Generalized volume loss with bilateral hippocampal atrophy, a pattern supporting Alzheimer disease in the right clinical setting. No infarct, mass or hemorrhage.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after neurology. Neurology letter and MRI reviewed with daughter: Alzheimer-type dementia, MMSE 18, hippocampal atrophy on MRI. Daughter tearful but not surprised given her aunt's course.
Donepezil 5 mg at night for six weeks: some loose stools the first week, now fine. No dizziness or slow pulse. Evenings still rough a few times a week.
Diabetes: no lows. Daughter now sets out the pills weekly and checks the insulin pen at night.
Exam: pulse regular in the 70s. Lungs without wheeze. No edema.
Plan: A1c, BMP today. Neurology follow-up next month for the dose increase. Gave daughter information on the local caregiver support group and adult day options. Advance directive conversation started; she wants her daughter as decision-maker - will formalize at the wellness visit.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Neurology follow-up, 3/8/2022. Ms. Mayhew returns with her daughter. Donepezil 5 mg tolerated after brief GI upset. Daughter sees no change in memory, slightly fewer evening outbursts. MRI reviewed: generalized and hippocampal atrophy, no vascular lesion of note. Exam unchanged, nonfocal. Plan: increase donepezil to 10 mg at bedtime. Follow up in 6 months or as needed. Medications otherwise as listed by PCP. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly wellness visit, daughter present for the whole visit.
Function: needs reminders for meals and meds; daughter or son stop by most days. Still dresses and bathes herself. No falls. Not driving since winter.
Mood: PHQ-2 1, not depressed per daughter, more 'quiet'.
Cognition: known Alzheimer's, on donepezil 10 since March.
Safety: stove use supervised; smoke detectors checked by son.
Prevention: mammogram due this fall (last one at 74). Vaccines current through the fall booster.
Exam: no distress, BP and weight as recorded. Chest without wheeze. RRR. Monofilament intact.
Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, urine microalbumin today. Yearly eye exam on schedule. Follow-up in 4-5 weeks for diabetes check (A1c deferred to then).

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Pelvic pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter brought her after Mom admitted to 'something falling down there.' Over about a year a heavy, dragging feeling in the pelvis, worse by evening, and she can feel a bulge when washing. Urine stream weak and she feels she never quite empties. No leakage of stool, no rectal bulge. No fever or burning.
Exam (chaperoned by MA): external exam shows vaginal tissue at the introitus at rest, more with bearing down. No ulceration visible. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable.
UA dip negative for infection.
Assessment: symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse with voiding difficulty.
Plan: gynecology referral. A1c also due - drawn today.

Addendum 6/1: A1c 7.8, a touch above her usual. Will look at it with her at the next diabetes visit; no change today.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Urogynecology/gynecology consult, date of service 6/28/2022. Thank you for this referral.
Ms. Mayhew is 74 and came with her daughter. Her neurologist diagnosed Alzheimer's disease in December. For about a year the pressure and the bulge have steadily progressed; she reports a slow stream and a sense of residual urine. She denies stool incontinence or anything protruding from the rectum. Not sexually active.
PMH: T2DM, HTN, COPD, CKD 3, hyperlipidemia, osteoporosis, CAD, gastroparesis, Alzheimer's. No prior surgery. Meds: metformin, glargine, lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, metoclopramide, donepezil. NKDA. Most recent A1c 7.8 (PCP, 5/31).
BP 145/90. BMI 32.
Pelvic exam: with straining, the cervix and both vaginal walls descend past the introitus. Cervix atrophic-appearing without ulceration or lesion. Last Pap normal.
Impression: severe symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse.
Discussion: surgical repair and pessary reviewed. She is clear that she wants to stay away from an operation; she is frightened of anesthesia and worries about her many medical problems. Daughter supports that.
Plan: pessary fitting visit in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Pessary fitting
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Pessary fitting 7/19/2022. A ring pessary with support was placed after trial of two sizes; retained with cough and walking around the office. She voided easily afterward with a stronger stream and said the heaviness was gone. Daughter shown what to watch for (bleeding, discharge, pain, trouble voiding). Office removal and cleaning about every 4 months. NKDA.

documents.title: Pessary update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: From Frances's daughter - just wanted you to know the pessary is working. Mom says she can pee 'like a normal person' again. Gyn will do the cleanings every 4 months, first one in November.

documents.title: Re: Pessary update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. Thanks for letting me know.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well with the pessary. Diabetes: May A1c 7.8. For someone her age with dementia I'm aiming for under 8 and avoiding lows; daughter agrees. No hypoglycemia.
Nausea now and then after bigger meals.
Exam: vitals reviewed; lungs clear without wheeze; regular heart; feet with good sensation, no wounds.
Plan: same regimen, A1c and BMP today. Flu and bivalent COVID at a nurse visit next month. Mammogram ordered (last screening one).

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu left arm and Pfizer bivalent booster right arm. No prior reactions beyond sore arm. Observed, discharged with daughter.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 2020. Breasts are heterogeneously fatty with scattered fibroglandular tissue. No new mass, suspicious calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Pessary check
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Pessary visit 11/16/2022. Ring pessary removed, cleaned and replaced. Vaginal walls without erosion or bleeding. Voiding well, no discharge. Next check in 4 months. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Abdominal pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three months of on-and-off upper belly pain, a dull ache she points to just under the breastbone, which she says goes 'straight through to my back.' Comes and goes, not clearly tied to meals. Weight steady, appetite the same, bowels the same. No vomiting, no black stools. Daughter had thought it was her usual stomach trouble.
Exam: no jaundice. Abdomen soft, not distended, mildly tender in the epigastrium, no mass, no rebound. Weight unchanged on our scale.
Assessment: epigastric pain radiating to the back, persistent. Gastroparesis does not quite fit the pattern.
Plan: hepatic panel and amylase today, abdominal ultrasound. Will call with results.

reports.text: Complete abdominal ultrasound. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. No biliary ductal dilatation; common bile duct normal caliber. In the head of the pancreas there is a cystic lesion measuring 4 cm with a thickened, irregular wall and calcifications. The main pancreatic duct is not visualized. Pancreatic body and tail partly obscured by bowel gas. Spleen normal. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm cystic lesion in the pancreatic head with a thickened irregular wall and calcifications. No biliary dilatation. Main pancreatic duct not seen. Further evaluation with gastroenterology recommended.

orders.reason: Pancreatic head cystic lesion with high-risk features

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called daughter (patient on speaker). Liver tests and amylase normal. Ultrasound shows a 4 cm cyst in the head of the pancreas with a thick, irregular wall and calcium in it. Explained that some pancreatic cysts are harmless and some are precancerous, and this one has features that need a specialist look. Urgent GI referral placed; they will likely want an MRI and possibly an endoscopic ultrasound. Daughter will take her to all appointments. Questions answered.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam letter
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Diabetic eye exam 11/30/2022, dilated. No diabetic retinopathy either eye. Cataracts early and stable. Next exam in a year. Allergies: none known.

conditions.label: Pancreatic cystic neoplasm with high-risk features

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology consultation, 12/19/2022.
Referred for a pancreatic head cyst. Ms. Mayhew (Alzheimer's dementia since December 2021, pelvic prolapse managed by gynecology since June) has had about three months of intermittent dull upper abdominal pain that travels to her back. No change in weight, appetite or bowel pattern.
History: diabetes and blood pressure are reasonably controlled on metformin, glargine and lisinopril; also HCTZ, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, metoclopramide, donepezil. NKDA. No surgeries. Mother had breast cancer. Former smoker, no alcohol.
Exam: abdomen soft, not distended, mild epigastric tenderness, no jaundice, no palpable mass.
Data: liver tests and amylase normal (PCP, 11/22). Ultrasound 11/29: 4 cm cystic lesion in the pancreatic head with thick, irregular wall and calcifications; no biliary dilatation; main duct not visualized.
Impression: pancreatic cystic neoplasm with high-risk imaging features.
Plan: MRI abdomen with MRCP, serum CA 19-9, then EUS with fine-needle aspiration for cyst fluid analysis and cytology. Depending on results, surgical opinion. Daughter understands the plan.

documents.title: MRI abdomen with MRCP
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside report, study date 1/17/2023, copy to PCP.
MRI abdomen with and without contrast and MRCP.
Pancreatic head: 4.0 cm cystic lesion with a thick enhancing wall and peripheral calcification. No solid enhancing component. Main pancreatic duct 4 mm. Common bile duct normal caliber without dilatation. Pancreatic body and tail otherwise unremarkable. Liver without focal lesion. No lymphadenopathy. No ascites.
Impression: 4.0 cm thick-walled cystic lesion of the pancreatic head with peripheral calcification. Recommend EUS correlation.
Serum CA 19-9 drawn same day: 22 U/mL (normal).

events.reason: EUS with FNA of pancreatic cyst

reports.text: Specimen: pancreatic head cyst, EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration. Received viscous fluid; cell block and smears prepared. Smears show thick mucinous material with scattered benign-appearing ductal epithelium and histiocytes. No atypical or malignant cells identified. Cyst fluid CEA 412 ng/mL.
reports.conclusion: Mucinous cyst contents. Negative for malignant cells. Elevated cyst fluid CEA (412 ng/mL).

documents.title: Endoscopic ultrasound with FNA
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
EUS with FNA, 2/14/2023, under monitored anesthesia care (patient anxious about sedation; reassured, tolerated well).
Findings: thick-walled cyst in the pancreatic head, about 4 cm, as on MRI, with peripheral calcification and no mural nodule or solid component seen. No ductal dilatation. FNA with a 22-gauge needle: viscous clear fluid aspirated, sent for CEA and cytology. No immediate complications.
Results: cyst fluid CEA 412 ng/mL; cytology mucinous material, no malignant cells.
Impression: mucinous pancreatic cystic neoplasm with high-risk features. Referral to pancreatic surgery for an opinion. NKDA.

documents.title: Pancreatic surgery consultation
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Surgical consultation, 3/14/2023. Seen with daughter and son.
Reviewed ultrasound, MRI/MRCP, EUS and cytology: 4.0 cm mucinous cyst of the pancreatic head with thick enhancing wall and calcification, CEA 412, cytology negative, CA 19-9 22. These are high-risk features and resection (pancreaticoduodenectomy) would usually be recommended in a fit patient.
Her context: 75, moderate Alzheimer's dementia, CAD, COPD, CKD 3, insulin-requiring diabetes, gastroparesis. Operative risk and recovery burden would be substantial.
She said plainly she does not want an operation and is afraid of anesthesia. Her children agree with her choice. She appeared to understand that she was declining surgery and why.
Plan: no surgery. Surveillance MRI/MRCP in 6 months with gastroenterology, then every 6-12 months depending on stability. Return to us if new symptoms, jaundice, weight loss or interval change. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reviewed the surgical letter with patient and daughter. Frances again said 'no operation' without hesitation; I think this is a sound and consistent choice for her. Surveillance MRI in September with GI.
Pain: belly ache much less often since the new year, maybe once every week or two, mild, no meds needed.
Diabetes/BP: no issues. EUS sedation went fine.
Exam: abdomen soft, minimal epigastric tenderness, no jaundice. Lungs without wheeze, regular rhythm.
Plan: A1c, BMP. Wellness visit in May; will do advance care planning then with both children if possible.

events.reason: Annual wellness visit, advance care planning

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and Advance Care Planning
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wellness visit with daughter; son joined by phone for the planning part.
Function: needs prompting for meals and pills, help with appointments and money; independent with toileting, dressing and walking. No falls this year. Pessary checks at gyn every 4 months.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance care planning (about 35 minutes): Frances can say what matters to her - staying in her own house, not being 'kept alive on machines', no big operations. Health care proxy form completed naming her daughter, son as alternate. She would want hospital treatment for things that can be fixed. MOLST not done today; family would like to think it over.
Exam: vitals as charted, lungs without wheeze, heart regular, no edema, feet intact.
Plan: yearly labs today. Fall vaccines in October. Copy of proxy to daughter and scanned.

documents.title: Pessary check
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Routine pessary check 7/18/2023. Patient with daughter, no complaints, no bleeding. Device removed and cleaned; mucosa intact, no ulceration. Reinserted, comfortable. Continue every 4 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Quiet summer. No lows. Belly pain rare. Breathing fine in the heat. Daughter reports the evening restlessness comes and goes.
Exam: unremarkable today apart from known findings; chest without wheeze, RRR, abdomen soft.
A1c and BMP drawn. Continue. GI surveillance MRI in September.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: GI follow-up, 9/12/2023. Surveillance MRI/MRCP 9/5/2023: pancreatic head cyst unchanged at 4.0 cm with thick wall and peripheral calcification; no solid component; main duct 4 mm, unchanged; no biliary dilatation. Clinically, abdominal pain now infrequent and mild. No weight loss or jaundice. Plan: continue surveillance, repeat MRI in about 9 months. Medications reviewed as per her list, including metoclopramide before meals for gastroparesis. NKDA.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP standing order: high-dose flu (L), updated COVID (R), RSV (L, 1 inch below flu site). Daughter consented with patient. Tolerated, no immediate reaction.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam letter
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic eye exam on 11/28/2023. No retinopathy, no macular edema. Mild cataracts unchanged. Next visit 1 year. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Tremor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter concerned about a change over the last few weeks: shaking in both hands at rest, right worse; she seems stiff getting up and slow at everything - takes ages to button a cardigan, needs help with cooking she used to manage. Daughter says her face looks 'blank' and she doesn't swing her arms when walking. No falls. Memory per daughter no different from summer.
Exam: reduced facial expression. Resting tremor of the right hand, slight on the left. Increased tone at both elbows and wrists. Walks slowly with short steps and little arm swing. Strength normal.
Assessment: new parkinsonism. She has been on metoclopramide for years - a likely culprit.
Plan: asked neurology to see her before the holidays if they can, since they know her; not changing meds until they weigh in.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology note, date of service 12/29/2023 (received 1/25/2024).
Ms. Mayhew, 75, known to our clinic since her Alzheimer's diagnosis in 2021, is back with progressive motor symptoms over the past month after a recent visit with her gastroenterologist. She has a resting tremor of the hands, stiffness, and slowness that interferes with cooking and dressing. Her daughter has noticed a fixed facial expression, less smiling, and diminished arm swing. No falls, hallucinations or change in mood. Cognition at her known baseline per daughter.
Medications: insulin glargine, metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, donepezil 10 mg, metoclopramide 10 mg three times daily before meals (several years). NKDA.
Exam: hypomimia, reduced blink rate, mild stooped posture. Cogwheel rigidity in both arms. Decreased arm swing bilaterally. Resting tremor right hand at about 4 Hz. Slow, short-stepped gait. Strength and reflexes normal, sensation intact.
Impression: drug-induced parkinsonism due to metoclopramide.
Plan: metoclopramide stopped today; daughter instructed. For gastroparesis, small frequent low-fat meals; no other prokinetic recommended from our side. Expect improvement over weeks to months. Return in about 4 months. Please update her medication list.
